QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_36

question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)?

answer.text: It is created by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and includes unpaid dividends, call money, and interest remaining unpaid and unclaimed for 7 years
It is created by SEBI and only covers mutual fund redemption proceeds
It is managed by RBI and used to compensate depositors in failed banks
It is operated by the depositories and pools unclaimed demat shares only

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) is created by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). Specified monies that remain unpaid and unclaimed for a period of 7 years -- such as unpaid dividends, call money, and interest -- form part of the IEPF. The Trap: The IEPF is an MCA-created fund, not a SEBI, RBI, or depository creation. Its scope, per the workbook, is unpaid/unclaimed amounts on the specified list after 7 years, not all unclaimed mutual fund redemption proceeds, bank deposits, or demat shares. Note: The 7-year unclaimed threshold is the trigger for items to form part of the IEPF. Any role of an RTA in transferring mutual fund units to the IEPF should be cited only from a direct, current source.
